instructions.question: What kind of knowledge is this section?
instructions.focus: Pick the single best bin. Use noise when the section should not be forced into a durable kind.

criteria.what: A recorded decision: the choice that was made, the context, and why that option won.
criteria.not_for: The current shape of the system with no recorded choice (architecture), or a rule that must stay true with no decision write-up (invariant).
examples: ADR 0001: We chose a local Hindsight bank.
We decided stable document ids so re-seed upserts.

criteria.what: A constraint that must remain true of the product or domain, independent of one write-up.
criteria.not_for: The record of how the team chose it (adr), or a contributor convention (standard).
examples: Secrets never leave the machine.
The bank id is not the Docker container name.

criteria.what: Caller-facing behavior: a CLI flag, command contract, or HTTP route that other people depend on.
criteria.not_for: The field list of a stored document (schema), or which module owns the code (architecture).
examples: seed --dry-run must not call Hindsight.
retain accepts content, document_id, and tags.

criteria.what: How the system is divided: modules, boundaries, and where a concern lives.
criteria.not_for: The decision record that chose the split (adr), or the steps an operator runs (runbook).
examples: Scanner, extractor, and seeder stay separate.
Commands must not own extraction.

criteria.what: An engineering convention the repository requires contributors to follow.
criteria.not_for: A personal formatting taste (style_pref), or a product constraint that is true even without a contributor (invariant).
examples: Throw NoccioloError and name the next step.
Prefer small, focused changes.

criteria.what: A repeated operator procedure: the commands, the order, and what success looks like.
criteria.not_for: Why the system is shaped that way (architecture), or a one-time choice (adr).
examples: Start Hindsight, then run nocciolo seed.
Run nocciolo prune after a doc path is deleted.

criteria.what: A data shape: field names, types, and allowed values for config or a payload.
criteria.not_for: What a command promises to do (public_api), or a narrative of module boundaries (architecture).
examples: .nocciolo/config.json requires bankId and provider.
Retain metadata includes source and knowledge_kind.

criteria.what: A personal taste about formatting, tone, or tools that the repository does not require.
criteria.not_for: A convention the repository requires (standard). Style preferences belong in a personal memory store later, not the company brain.
examples: I like a two-space indent in scratch notes.
I prefer this editor theme for markdown.

criteria.what: Background for how the project got here, without stating a rule that is still in force.
criteria.not_for: A decision that still applies (adr), or the structure as it works now (architecture).
examples: The first prototype stored one JSON file.
Prune shipped after the scanner.

criteria.what: A view or judgment that the project has not adopted as a decision, standard, or invariant.
criteria.not_for: A recorded choice (adr), a required convention (standard), or a personal formatting taste (style_pref).
examples: This API might feel heavy later, and we have not decided to change it.
I would rather not add another provider yet.

criteria.what: Text that is not durable project knowledge, including a changelog, table of contents, badge wall, generated dump, meeting notes, or a TODO pile.
criteria.not_for: Any durable bin above. Noise is skipped and is not forced into a durable kind.
examples: A changelog entry for 0.1.3.
A table of contents with no decision.
